newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin, Lafontaine discuss Maastricht change-paper.
newsitem.headline: Jospin, Lafontaine discuss Maastricht change-paper.

text.p: France's Socialist Party leader Lionel Jospin and Germany's Social Democratic Party (SPD) leader Oskar Lafontaine are discussing easing a key condition for European monetary union, according to newsletter La Lettre d'Expansion.

The weekly newsletter, in an unsourced and brief item, said the talks were aimed at raising the Maastricht Treaty ceiling of three percent of GDP for budget deficits in 1998 to 3.5 percent or even 3.7 percent.
It also said that the two party leaders were working on the creation of an "economic government" which would control the European central bank.
At the Socialist Party in Paris there was no immediate comment.
Lionel Jospin is due to give a radio interview later on Monday morning as part of the run-up to the snap parliamentary election of May 25 and June 1.
The Socialist Party has so far said that it wants to have Italy, Spain and Portugal in the first round of countries joining the euro single currency.

Senior party representatives have also said they want the Maastricht criteria to be applied as "trends" instead of absolute figures and they have also said they favour an "economic government" for Europe.

The Socialist Party has said it wants to renegotiate Maastricht if it came to power. It wants the single currency but under conditions. It also wants a EU pact of solidarity and growth to help create jobs and believes the euro should not be overvalued compared with the dollar.
